contents.support: The actual relative Clifford symbol and product formula are inspected. Theorem 11.5 invokes the already-known orthogonal periodicity/KO groups; it is not used as its own real Bott supplier.

contents.name: Spin and Spin-c Thom classes, §12
contents.support: The source statement distinguishes real and quaternionic spinor types and gives the rank conditions. Its classifying argument is restated locally with exact hypotheses; it is not treated as a complete local proof.

sources.title: M. F. Atiyah, K-Theory (lectures, notes by D. W. Anderson, 1967), with K-Theory and Reality reprint
sources.locator: Complete 220-page PDF. Read §§1.3, 2.2 and 2.7 of K-Theory (PDF pp.13–18, 44–65, 98–116) and the appended K-Theory and Reality paper §§2–4 (PDF pp.207–219 / printed pp.374–386).

contents.name: Vector bundle complements and complex K-theory preliminaries, §§1.3 and 2.2
contents.support: The metric, orthogonal complement and bundle Grothendieck constructions were inspected. The main lecture notes explicitly develop complex bundles; no real theorem is inferred from the complex sections.

contents.name: Complex K Thom class and finite-CW argument, §2.7
contents.support: The exterior-algebra symbol and local-to-global finite-CW/splitting-principle route were read in full. The local Spin-c proof supplies the equivariance and Clifford fiber details.

contents.name: K-Theory and Reality, §§2–4, alternate KO periodicity route
contents.support: The full KR exactness and Clifford coefficient proof was inspected. This is a valid comparison route through KR and complex Bott, but the owner construction requires proving real Bott from the locally established real Clifford–Thom map; this alternate route is not a premise.

sources.title: Alexei Kitaev, Periodic table for topological insulators and superconductors (2009)
sources.locator: Complete 9-page text. Read the abstract, Table 1 and Table 2, the finite Dirac-operator/mass discussion (PDF pp.2–8), and “The effect of interaction” (PDF p.8).

contents.name: Tenfold symmetry table and Clifford classifying spaces, Tables 1–2
contents.support: The real/complex index order, strong invariant entries, and classifying spaces were compared. The local theorem is restricted to the specified finite Dirac-mass extension problem.

contents.name: Local gapped Hamiltonian texture theorem, §4
contents.support: The paper states its broad local/disordered equivalence theorem but explicitly says its key technical proof cannot be explained in the short note. No such general claim is included as a supplier.

contents.name: Strong versus weak invariants and interaction caveat, Table 2 and “The effect of interaction”
contents.support: The torus weak-invariant contribution and the eight-chain interaction counterexample were inspected; the companion records the scope boundary without claiming general interaction stability.

sources.title: John W. Milnor and James D. Stasheff, Characteristic Classes (Princeton University Press, 1974)
sources.locator: §4, Example 4 and Theorem 4.5, PDF pp.47–50 / printed pp.43–46; the section derives w(T RP^n)=(1+a)^(n+1). The section explicitly treats existence of the Stiefel–Whitney classes as an axiom at this point and postpones its proof; that dependency is not imported.

contents.name: Tangent Stiefel–Whitney class of real projective space
contents.support: Example 4 identifies T RP^n as Hom(γ,γ^⊥); Theorem 4.5 gives w(T RP^n)=(1+a)^(n+1). At n=2 this implies w1=3a=a≠0 over Z/2. The local carrier remains escalated because the exact projective-bundle definition/existence supplier is missing.
